full_judgment: 2. The facts relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal are that the petitioner herein as plaintiff-instituted Civil Suit No. 19 of 2006 before the Joint District Judge, Court No. 4, Dhaka for declaration of title of 1.98½ acres land described in "Lime schedule to the plaint and cancellation of partition deed No. 9442 dated 27-11-1995. The case was transferred to the Court of Joint. District Judge, Court No. 5, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 467 of 2010. The plaintiff contended, inter alia, that Zinnat Ali, Ashraf Ali and Rokon Ali were the owners of land measuring 6.32 acres in CS Khatian No. 49 and SA Khatian No. 571, and after their death the names of their heirs Shahebjan Bibi and others were duly recorded in SA Khatian for 6.32 acres land and in RS Khatian 3.75 acres land was recorded in their names. As per record Shukur Ali transferred 96 decimals land in the name of his son Ali Akbar on 4-11-1970 by registered heba-bil-ewaj deed No. 16684 and Ali Akbar became owner of that land. In addition, RS recorded owner Abed Ali transferred 15 decimals land in the name of Ali Akbar by registered deed No. 4718 on 19-2-1974 in Touji No.330, Mouza-Dogair, CS Khatian No. 49 plot No. 1192 and in the same Khatian in plot Nos. 1185 and 1178 he jointly with his father purchased 37 decimals land on 21-6-1977 by registered deed No. 18184. He purchased 58 decimals land on 31-8-1987 by registered deed No. 9120 from Sobed Ali and Badsha Miah. All the above land was not ejmali property and the plaintiff was enjoying the same, but the land was mistakenly included in partition deed No. 9442. After the death of his mother his father Md Sukkur Ali married Shahana Khatun and defendants Nos. 2-8 and 11 are the step brothers and sisters of the plaintiff and after his father's death the defendant No. 1 kept all the registered deeds in his custody and it was not known to the plaintiff and, thereafter, on 27-11-1995 all the defendants manufactured a partition deed by stating that they have divided the land of Sukkur Ali among themselves but fraudulently they divided the land of the plaintiff and obtained his signature when he was suffering from serious fever and physical complications. The property was not the ejmali property and the plaintiff owned and possessed the same exclusively. Beyond the knowledge' of the plaintiff, the said property was incorporated in the partition deed No. 9442 registered on 27-114995. After the plaintiff got cured, his stepmother gave him the deed in question and then he requested the defendants for rectification of the deed, but the defendants did not pay any heed. Hence, the plaintiff filed the suit.
